title: In utero electroporation and cranial window implantation for in vivo wide-field two-photon calcium imaging using G-CaMP9a transgenic mice
protocol: Prepare glass capillaries using a puller.
Break the tip of the capillaries with fine forceps to achieve an approximate diameter of 50 μm.
Irradiate pulled glass capillaries with U.V. for 15 minutes before use.
Add 1/20 volume of 1.0% Fast Green dye to the plasmid solution used for injection.
Fill the glass capillary with the dyed plasmid solution.
Purify the plasmid solution using an endotoxin-free kit.
Attach the glass capillary to the suction tube.
Suck up 10 μL of plasmid solution.
Anesthetize a pregnant mouse (E15.5) with an intraperitoneal injection of an anesthetic mixture at 100 μL per 10 g of body weight.
Wait 10 min to ensure the mouse is anesthetized by checking for pedal reflex and steady breathing.
Administer carprofen dissolved in saline (5.0 mg/kg-BW, subcutaneously) to relieve pain.
Administer dexamethasone dissolved in saline (2.0 mg/Kg-BW, intraperitoneally) to reduce inflammation.
Place the mouse on its back on the operating table.
Fix the limbs with surgical tape.
Place the pregnant mouse on an operating table with a heating pad.
Secure the mouse limbs using styrofoam platforms and surgical tape.
Warm the mouse on a heating pad at 37°C during surgery.
Apply white petrolatum ointment to protect the eyes.
Sterilize the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Remove hairs from the abdominal area with a razor.
Make a ∼30-mm-long midline incision through the skin and abdominal wall using fine scissors, avoiding the nipples.
Cover the abdomen with sterilized gauze containing a central slit.
Wet the gauze with warm saline (40°C) using a transfer pipette.
Attach a ring forceps to the uterus at a gap between embryos.
Carefully pull the uterus out of the abdominal cavity.
Immediately wet the exposed uterus with warm saline.
Inject 1 μL plasmid solution into the lateral ventricles of the embryos by exhalation.
Insert the capillary vertically into the lateral ventricles, approximately 1 mm depth from the uterine wall.
Hold the plasmid-injected head of the embryo with forceps-type electrodes.
Deliver five electric pulses with an electroporator.
Ensure the anode points towards the targeted cortical area.
Clean the electrodes, especially the platinum tip.
Verify air bubbles appear on the electrode surface in saline during pulse delivery.
Use a voltage between 25–35 V for electroporation.
Consider using a 5 mm or 3 mm platinum disk electrode as alternatives.
Return the uterus carefully into the abdominal cavity.
Fill the abdominal cavity with warm saline using a transfer pipette.
Suture the abdominal cavity with a microneedle holder and surgical needle.
Suture the skin with a microneedle holder and surgical needle.
Administer atipamezole hydrochloride (0.75 mg/kg-BW, intraperitoneally) to reverse anesthesia.
Remove the surgical tape from the mouse.
Transfer the mouse to a clean recovery cage.
Warm the mouse on a heating pad at 37°C until it recovers from the anesthetic.
Transfer the mouse back to its original cage.
Transfer the mouse from the chamber to the mouse adaptor.
Anesthetize the mouse with 1.5%–2.0% isoflurane and 1.0 L/min airflow.
Inject carprofen (dissolved in saline; 5.0 mg/kg-BW, subcutaneously) for pain relief.
Inject dexamethasone (dissolved in saline; 2.0 mg/Kg-BW, intraperitoneally) for inflammation relief.
Apply white petrolatum ointment to the eyes for protection.
Trim the hair on the scalp with fine scissors.
Apply hair-removal cream over the trimmed scalp and wait 5 min.
Clean off residual hair and hair-removal cream using small cotton tips.
Ensure no residue of hair-removal cream remains on the eyes.
Apply 70% ethanol over the trimmed scalp for sterilization.
Wash off any remaining hair and hair-removal cream with small cotton tips.
Secure the head in a mouse adaptor by engaging ear bars.
Apply superglue on a titanium headplate.
Attach the headplate with superglue.
Glue the headplate with dental acrylic on the headplate.
Glue the headplate with dental acrylic to the skull by filling the space under the headplate and exposing the skull.
Mark the area where the cranial window will be made.
Drill the skull inside of the circle marked previously.
Peel away the thinned skull with fine forceps.
Clean the dura.
Place the coverglass and press it with a toothpick.
Apply surgical superglue to the edge of the coverglass.
Apply dental acrylic surrounding the coverglass.
Dry the dental acrylic completely.
Apply lidocaine jelly over the trimmed scalp for local anesthesia using small cotton tips.
Wait 5 min for local anesthesia.
Incise the scalp.
Open the skin above the skull (∼30 mm) with a fine scissor.
Cut the scalp skin (∼30 mm) on both sides of the incision.
Push remaining skin to the side with small cotton tips.
Scratch the exposed skull with fine forceps.
Apply superglue to the titanium headplate.
Attach a custom-made titanium headplate to the skull with superglue.
Keep pushing the headplate from the top to get firmly attached to the cranium.
Wait at least 10 minutes for the superglue to dry completely.
Glue the headplate with dental acrylic by filling the space under the headplate and exposing the skull.
Cover all exposed bone to prevent infection.
Detach the mouse from the adaptor if the ear bars block the space below the headplate.
Continue filling dental acrylic under the headplate while holding the mouse in your hand.
Wait 10 minutes for the dental acrylic to dry completely.
Drill the skull inside of the circle made in step 39 using a speed between 3,000–5,000 rpm.
Thin the skull until there is a small crack or it can be easily pushed with fine forceps.
Cool and clean the thinned skull periodically with saline.
Gently spray the thinned area periodically with compressed air to prevent overheating.
Peel away the thinned skull gently with fine forceps when some cracks are visible.
Stop bleeding immediately if it occurs using a gelatin sponge moistened with saline.
Clean the dura with a gelatin sponge moisturized with saline by a transfer pipette.
Make sure no bleeding occurs when adding a drop of saline to the dura.
Place the coverglass on the dura pressing on its center with a toothpick, and make sure there is no bleeding.
Clean the coverslip with 70% ethanol and sterilize them with U.V. light before use.
Do not proceed if bleeding starts; remove the coverglass and clean the dura with a gelatin sponge moisturized with saline.
Press on the center of the coverglass with a toothpick while applying surgical superglue (Aron alpha A) to the edge of the coverglass using a blunt needle.
Wait 10 min for the surgical superglue to dry completely.
Ensure that the surgical superglue completely seals the glass periphery; if not, apply an additional seal.
Apply dental acrylic to hide the exposed cranium except for the coverglass.
Wait 10 minutes for the dental acrylic to dry completely.
Apply silicone sealant to protect the exposed region from light.
Remove the mouse from the mouse adaptor.
Transfer the anesthetized mouse to a clean recovery cage.
Warm the mouse on a heating pad at 37°C until it recovers from anesthesia.
After waking up, transfer the mouse to its original cage.
